metadata.archetype_justification: Application has a SQL Server database with read and write operations (INSERT INTO timesheets, SELECT queries) and entity lifecycle management (employee timesheet entries), classifying it as stateful-crud.

tech_stack.architecture: Monolithic WebForms with SQL Server backend

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application is an ASP.NET WebForms UI with no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration would require direct database access or UI automation (RPA). There are no API endpoints — only server-rendered .aspx pages with postback-driven interactions.
findings.gap: No programmatic API exists. The only integration path is direct SQL or UI automation.
findings.recommendation: Extract data access logic into a service layer and expose as a REST API (e.g., ASP.NET Web API or modern framework).

blocker_remediation.immediate: Extract data access logic from Timesheet.aspx.vb into a service layer and expose as a REST API.
blocker_remediation.target_state: A documented REST API with endpoints for timesheet CRUD operations.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses ASP.NET Forms Authentication with session cookies. There is no support for service accounts, OAuth2 client credentials, API keys, or mTLS. The only authentication mechanism is human-interactive browser-based login.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. An agent cannot authenticate without simulating a browser login flow.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication for programmatic access with principal attribution.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Implement API key or OAuth2 client credentials authentication for programmatic access.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Machine identities with attributed principals that authenticate without browser interaction.

findings.title: Plaintext Credentials in Configuration
findings.description: Database credentials are stored in plaintext in web.config (User ID=ts_app;Password=Time2006!). No secrets management system exists. No rotation mechanism. The README confirms this is a known issue.
findings.gap: Credentials hardcoded in configuration committed to version control. No rotation. A source code leak would expose the database password.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Remove plaintext credentials from web.config.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Move connection string credentials to an encrypted configuration section or secrets management service.
blocker_remediation.target_state: All credentials managed via secrets management with automated rotation. No plaintext secrets in source.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: Single database user (ts_app) for all operations. No role-based access control, no IAM policies, no API Gateway resource policies. All authenticated users share identical database privileges.
findings.gap: No mechanism to scope down agent access per capability. Single shared credential grants full access.
findings.recommendation: Introduce role-based authorization with distinct permission scopes (read vs write, own-data vs all-data).

compensating_controls: Implement row-level filtering by employee ID
Create separate database users with different permission levels

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Any authenticated user can both read and write timesheet entries. The code does not distinguish between read and write permissions.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict a caller to read-only within the same resource type.
findings.recommendation: Add action-level authorization checks (role-based decorators or middleware) distinguishing read vs write permissions per caller.

compensating_controls: Add role checks before write operations
Implement database-level permissions with separate users

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. No CloudTrail, no application-level audit logs, no principal logging for operations.
findings.gap: No immutable, tamper-evident audit trail. Cannot determine who performed what action.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging (CloudTrail for infrastructure, application-level structured audit logs shipped to immutable storage).

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, audit logging important but not deployment blocker for read-only agents.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Read-only agents do not execute write operations, so immutable audit trails are important for system maturity but not a deployment blocker.
compensating_controls: Add application-level logging of all operations with caller identity

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Mechanism
findings.description: No mechanism exists to suspend or revoke individual agent identities. The application has no concept of machine identities, API keys, or service accounts that could be individually disabled.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent identity without disrupting the entire application.
findings.recommendation: Implement an identity system supporting per-agent credential revocation (API keys with disable endpoints, or Cognito user pool).

compensating_controls: Implement API key-based auth with per-key revocation
Use external identity provider with user-level disable

findings.title: No Sensitive Data Scoping
findings.description: Employee-specific data (employee_id, hours, project, entry_date) stored in SQL Server without field-level scoping or access control differentiation. All fields returned in all queries.
findings.gap: No response scoping, no access control differentiation, no classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement field-level scoping and access control differentiation when building the API layer.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, B1 fires as RISK-SAFETY (sensitive fields returned in general queries under read-only scope).
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 B1 fired because SELECT returns all fields (employee_id, hours, project) without scoping. Under read-only scope, this resolves to RISK-SAFETY rather than BLOCKER.

b1.reasoning: All fields returned in SELECT without scoping; under read-only scope resolves to RISK-SAFETY.

b2.reasoning: No access control differentiation — single DB user for all operations.

compensating_controls: Limit query results to only fields necessary for agent tasks
Implement OAuth scopes separating data domains

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: SQL Server at IP 10.0.6.15 with no data residency documentation, GDPR references, or region-specific configurations. Employee work records may be subject to labor regulations.
findings.gap: No data residency controls or documentation. No constraints preventing cross-jurisdiction data transmission.
findings.recommendation: Classify employee timesheet data for residency requirements and implement controls preventing cross-jurisdiction transmission to LLM endpoints.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, data residency relevant but lower risk when no data modification occurs.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Under read-only scope, data residency is evaluated as RISK-SAFETY rather than BLOCKER because the risk profile is lower when no data modification occurs.
compensating_controls: Implement data egress controls at network level

findings.title: PII Exposure in Error Output
findings.description: customErrors mode='Off' in web.config exposes detailed error messages including stack traces. SQL queries with embedded employee IDs would be displayed in error responses.
findings.gap: No PII redaction in error output. Disabled custom errors exposes internal details including SQL with user data.
findings.recommendation: Enable customErrors mode='RemoteOnly' immediately. Implement structured error handling that never exposes raw SQL or user identifiers.

compensating_controls: Enable custom errors to suppress detailed error information
Implement structured error handling that sanitizes output

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No structured error responses. customErrors mode='Off' exposes raw ASP.NET exception pages. No error codes, error bodies, or retryable indicators.
findings.gap: No machine-readable error classification exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON error responses with error codes, messages, and retryable indicators when building the REST API.

findings.title: State Not Queryable via API
findings.description: Current state is internally queryable via SELECT in BindGrid() but not exposed via a programmatic API. Only accessible through rendered HTML grid.
findings.gap: State not accessible via programmatic API for agent consumption.
findings.recommendation: Expose GET endpoints for resource state when building the API surface.

findings.title: No Pagination or Filtering
findings.description: SELECT query has no pagination (no LIMIT/OFFSET), minimal filtering (employee_id only), and fixed sorting (ORDER BY entry_date DESC). Result sets unbounded.
findings.gap: No pagination, limited filtering, fixed sorting. Unbounded result sets.
findings.recommendation: Implement pagination (limit/offset or cursor-based) and filter parameters when building the API.

findings.title: No Input Validation
findings.description: Zero input validation. btnSave_Click directly concatenates user input (txtDate.Text, txtHours.Text, txtProject.Text) into SQL strings without validation, type checking, or sanitization. SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.gap: Raw user input concatenated into SQL. No validation. No structured error responses for invalid input.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries and input validation (type checking, range validation, format validation) with structured error responses.

findings.title: Limited Temporal Metadata
findings.description: Only entry_date exists. No created_at or updated_at timestamps. No timezone handling visible. No Cache-Control headers. No freshness signaling.
findings.gap: Limited temporal metadata. No update tracking. No timezone normalization. No freshness indicators.
findings.recommendation: Add created_at and updated_at fields with UTC timezone storage when modernizing the schema.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema documentation, versioning, or breaking change detection. Schema visible only through inline SQL strings. No migration files, no schema registry.
findings.gap: No versioned schemas or contracts. Agent tool bindings would break silently on changes.
findings.recommendation: Document schema formally and implement API versioning when REST API is built.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing (no X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry), no structured logging (no JSON logs, no correlation IDs). Zero observability instrumentation.
findings.gap: Cannot trace or debug any request through the system.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON logging with correlation IDs and integrate distributed tracing (X-Ray or OpenTelemetry).

findings.title: No Alerting Configuration
findings.description: No alerting exists. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring integration. System degradation would go undetected.
findings.gap: No alerting on error rates or latency.
findings.recommendation: Implement alerting thresholds when modernizing infrastructure.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC exists. Manual deployment to single IIS 6 server on Windows Server 2003 via Visual Studio publish to network share.
findings.gap: Infrastructure entirely manual. No IaC governance, no change review, no drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure as code (Terraform or CloudFormation) when migrating off Windows Server 2003.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Manual Visual Studio publish. No automated testing of any kind. No contract testing.
findings.gap: No automated testing or API contract change detection.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with automated build, test, and deployment. Include API contract testing.

items.summary: Resolve all BLOCKERs (API surface, machine identity, credential management) and address critical RISK-SAFETY findings (authorization, audit logging, data classification, PII exposure).
Address RISK-QUALITY findings: structured errors, observability, schema versioning, input validation, and engineering maturity.
Address remaining INFO items as capacity allows to improve agent effectiveness.

recommended_actions.action: Build REST API layer with machine identity authentication
recommended_actions.rationale: The application has no programmatic API surface and no machine identity — agents cannot integrate at all without these foundational capabilities.
Plaintext credentials in web.config represent an immediate security vulnerability exploitable via source code leak or prompt injection.

recommended_actions.action: Implement role-based authorization with audit logging
recommended_actions.rationale: Authorization and audit controls are required for safe agent operation — without them, agent access cannot be scoped or monitored.

recommended_actions.action: Implement data classification and PII protection
recommended_actions.rationale: Employee data requires classification, residency controls, and PII protection before agent access is safe.
Observability and deployment maturity are required for operational confidence in agent-integrated systems.
